neighbours.label: relative pronoun ' who' / ' where' (also 'whoever') opening a relative clause right after its head noun
fire: Everyone at the wedding thanked the priest who led the service so warmly.
My cousin finally met the surgeon who repaired his knee last spring.
Police are still looking for the driver who caused the crash on Friday.
The judge spoke to the witness who had seen the robbery from her window.
We visited the small town where my father worked as a young teacher.
They returned to the beach where they had first met twenty years ago.
A reward was offered to the person who found the missing painting.
Le maire a remercié le pompier qui a sauvé les enfants de l'incendie.
quiet: Everyone at the wedding thanked the priest for leading the service so warmly.
My cousin finally met his surgeon after the knee operation last spring.
Police are still looking for a blue van seen near the crash on Friday.
The judge spoke briefly to the witness and then adjourned the hearing.
We visited the small town to see the school and the old church square.
They returned to the beach for a quiet walk after twenty years apart.
A reward was offered for any information about the missing painting.
Le maire a remercié les pompiers pour leur courage pendant l'incendie.

notes: Probe (fraction of max): 'the nurse who answered' 0.37, 'village where' 0.22, 'Whoever' 0.21, relative 'that' after 'printer' only 0.15 (peak elsewhere), complementizer 'said that' 0.07, demonstrative 'that movie' 0.08. Label narrowed to who/where after a head noun because relative 'that' scored low in probe despite top card example. Fire items follow the 'the <person noun> who <verb>' frame that scored highest; near misses keep topic and drop the relative clause.
